newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai police chief transferred amid scandals.
newsitem.headline: Thai police chief transferred amid scandals.

text.p: Thailand's police chief was removed from office on Friday amid a series of scandals involving the police department.

Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh summoned Pochana Boonyachinda to his residence and told him he was being transferred to a less active position in the interior ministry, spokesman Amnaj Chanawong told Reuters.
But police sources said Pochana had submitted his resignation to the police department soon after receiving the order.
Pochana was not available for comment.
Interior Minister Sanoh Thienthong said at a news conference that Pochana was being removed to "improve" the 200,000-strong police force.
"I am not bullying him (Pochana) but the government issued the order for his transfer to improve the working of the police force," he said.

He added that one of Pochana's four deputies, Pracha Promnok, who is in charge of the crime supression division, would be acting police chief until the Police Commission appointed a new national head later.

The police department has been under heavy criticism in recent weeks following several scandals, including allegations that police summarily executed six detained drug-trafficking suspects last month.

A recent study released by the Chulalongkorn University accused several senior police officers of taking bribes from underworld forces which run Thailand's multi-billion-dollar prostitution, drug trafficking and illegal gambling rackets.
